artworks.title: Gravure en Taille-douce: pl. III
artworks.artist: Antonio Baratta after A.-J. de Fehrt
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: This is a drawing demonstrating various engraving techniques. It includes figures labeled from 1 to 13 showing different stages and methods used in intaglio printing. The upper part displays outlines and profiles of human heads to illustrate depth creation through incision tools. In the middle, hands are depicted using engraving tools to showcase effective handling techniques. Below, there are diagrams of line and shading effects achieved in engraving, featuring crosshatching and parallel-line patterns. The artwork is annotated with letters and numbers to guide viewers through the engraving process.

artworks.title: Gravure en Taille-Douce: pl. IV
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: The image contains multiple sections showing different artistic engravings. In the top left and right corners, there are two oval portraits of a person's head and shoulders. The lower left corner features anatomical drawings of an arm and hand with labeled parts. The central section includes another oval portrait, with the subject looking upwards, and in historic attire. The bottom right corner shows a muscular figure poised as though swinging a large club. French text appears below the engravings.

artworks.title: Gravure, Maniere de faire mordre à l'eau-forte: pl. V
artworks.artist: Antonio Baratta after A.-J. de Fehrt
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: This is a drawing of various equipment and illustrations related to the process of etching. The image features detailed diagrams of different tools and processes used in etching, including a stand with a basin, sheets with intricate patterns, a lush landscape scene, and components like plates, measuring devices, and a box with bottles. Figures labeled from 1 to 7 signify each component or stage, presenting a clear instructional diagram of the etching process with accompanying French descriptions.

artworks.title: Gravure à l'Eau Forte, Machine à Balotter: pl. VI
artworks.artist: French 18th Century, and Denis Diderot, Jacques Renaud Benard
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: This is a technical illustration featuring components of a mechanical machine. The drawing shows different views and parts of the apparatus, with labels indicating items such as gears, rollers, and levers. The image includes figures detailing the drum, rods, a table, internal mechanisms, crossbars, brackets, a press, and a tray. The drawing is detailed and precise, showcasing the complexity and functionality of the machinery.

artworks.title: Gravure en Maniere Noire: pl. VII
artworks.artist: Antonio Baratta after A.-J. de Fehrt
artworks.medium: engraving, etching, and mezzotint on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: This is a drawing of various engraving tools and techniques used in the "Maniere Noire" or mezzotint process. The drawing shows detailed illustrations of engraving tools numbered as figures 1 through 7, including burnishers and roulettes, which are depicted with precision and labeled with letters indicating parts and possibly instructions for use. Below the tools are geometric grids labeled Fig. 000 and Seconde Fig. 000, showing a grid system with lines and numbers for alignment or scaling purposes. In the bottom right corner is Fig. 9, a small shaded illustration of a sphere inside a box or open-faced cube, showcasing the chiaroscuro effect achievable through the engraving technique. The inscriptions "Gravure en Maniere Noire" and "Pl. VII" suggest this is an educational or instructional plate on mezzotint engraving.

artworks.title: Gravure en Maniere de Crayon: pl. VIII
artworks.artist: Antonio Baratta after A.-J. de Fehrt
artworks.medium: engraving and crayon-manner engraving on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: This is a drawing showing various engraving tools and techniques. It includes detailed illustrations of tools like styluses, rollers, and other implements used in engraving. The drawings also show textural effects such as cross-hatching and stippling. There are anatomical drawings of the human ear, with contour lines and cross-hatching for depth. Labels and annotations indicate it may be an educational diagram on engraving techniques.

artworks.title: Gravure en Bois, Outils: pl. II
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: This is an image displaying a variety of woodworking tools. Each tool is labeled with a figure number for systematic organization, likely for instructional purposes. The tools include chisels, drills, calipers, and other devices used in wood engraving. The drawing is intricately detailed, emphasizing the precision and functionality of each tool with lines and shading. The title at the bottom indicates that it is related to wood engraving tools.

artworks.title: Gravure en Bois, Principes: pl. III
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: This is a drawing of wood engraving techniques. The drawing shows various techniques and examples of wood engraving, with different figures labeled and detailed. It includes multiple carvings and patterns, such as straight and curved lines, grids, and waveforms. Each figure demonstrates a different style or method of engraving on a block of wood. The final figure displays a detailed scene featuring an obelisk and classical architecture.

artworks.title: Imprimerie en Taille Douce, Devéloppement de la Presse: pl. II
artworks.artist: French 18th Century after Robert Benard and Louis-Jacques Goussier
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring detailed components of a printing press. The illustration includes various labeled parts and sectional views of mechanical structures related to a vintage printing press. Each component is shown with precise detail, likely indicating how different pieces fit together or function within the mechanism. The components are numbered and organized neatly across the page, with an emphasis on technical understanding. The etching style and the language used at the bottom ("Imprimerie en Taille Douce, Devéloppement de la Presse") suggest that this diagram serves as an instructional or descriptive guide for the assembly or function of the printing press depicted.

artworks.title: La Belle au bois dormant
artworks.medium: collotype in black on wove paper
artworks.dimensions:
plate: 12.5 x 22.2 cm (4 15/16 x 8 3/4 in.)
sheet (program closed): 17.2 x 27.5 cm (6 3/4 x 10 13/16 in.)
sheet (program opened): 17.2 x 55 cm (6 3/4 x 21 5/8 in.)
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Martin and Liane W. Atlas
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a theatre program for "La Belle au Bois Dormant." The announcement includes details about the performance, such as the creators and contributors, a quote from Shakespeare, the cast members, and the theater's address. The vintage program showcases elegant typography, offering a glimpse into the theatrical culture of the 1893-94 season at "Théâtre de L'Oeuvre."

artworks.title: Carmosine
artworks.medium: glyptograph on simili-japon paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Martin and Liane W. Atlas
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a theatre program for the play "Carmosine." The program features an embossed image on the left side with a figure in a long dress standing in a natural setting with foliage and trees around. On the right side, there is finely printed text listing details of the performance, including the cast, production team, and costume designers. The title "Carmosine," event date (June 10, 1895), and location are prominently displayed. The drawing includes delicate lines, a sophisticated layout, and a vintage aesthetic. The program is signed by Maurice Dumont in red at the bottom right.

artworks.title: Le Roi Candaule
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Martin and Liane W. Atlas
artworks.description: This is a theater program cover for the play "Le Roi Candaule" by André Gide. On the left side, there is a sketch with simplified and abstracted forms showing figures in an intricate scene. One figure appears thoughtful, potentially observing or interacting with another, while a minimally outlined third figure may be gesturing or positioned in the background. The sketch style is loose with sweeping lines, conveying a sense of motion or drama. The right side contains program information for the play in black text, listing characters, performers, and decorative elements separating text sections.

artworks.title: La Comédie de l'amour
artworks.medium: lithograph in green-black on wove paper (proof before letters at lower right and along right margin)
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Martin and Liane W. Atlas
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a group of characters with a theatrical theme. The scene shows several characters in expressive poses, potentially illustrating a narrative or scene from a theatre production. Each character is depicted with sketchy line-work conveying motion and emotion, and unique attire enhancing the theatrical atmosphere. Textual elements in the drawing suggest a connection to a play, with phrases like "La Comédie de l’Amour par Henrik Ibsen" and "Théâtre de l'Œuvre" hinting at a theatrical event. The artwork captures a theatrical narrative with a focus on character expression.

artworks.title: La Comédie de l'amour
artworks.medium: collotype in green-black on simili-japon paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Martin and Liane W. Atlas
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a promotional poster for a theatrical performance. The image shows expressive characters drawn in a sketchy, illustrative style. The left side features an older figure in a striped outfit next to text referencing "La Comédie de l'Amour" by Henrik Ibsen. In the center, two figures are conversing, one with long hair and a coat. On the right, there is a character resembling a soldier in a pose indicating authority or mockery. The drawing is surrounded by text detailing the theater information at the "Théâtre de l'Œuvre." The artwork aims to capture the theatrical and comedic essence of the production with dynamic lines and shading portraying movement and drama.

artworks.title: Fausta
artworks.medium: lithograph in brown on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Martin and Liane W. Atlas
artworks.description: The image shows a woman in flowing garment, standing with one arm raised as she adjusts the fabric around her. She has subtle facial features and dark, slightly mussed hair. Her clothing appears light and ethereal, draping around her form. She holds an object or fabric in her hand, adding to the sense of movement. The background features a textured surface, and text on the left side provides information about a theatrical production.

artworks.title: Le Chariot de terre cuite
artworks.medium: lithograph in blue and pink on wove paper [proof]
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Martin and Liane W. Atlas
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a theatrical program for "Le Chariot de Terre Cuite". The drawing features an illustration centered around a classical column and a human figure in traditional attire. The program details are listed within a bordered section on the left side, surrounded by stylized flowers and decorative vines. Below the figure, there are characters that appear to be Hindu script. The overall aesthetic is highly illustrative, reminiscent of the Art Nouveau style with delicate lines and ornate embellishments.

artworks.title: Des Mots! Des Mots!
artworks.medium: lithograph in brown on green wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Martin and Liane W. Atlas
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a scene showing individuals in a theatrical or educational setting. The image has a minimalistic sketch style with a monochromatic color palette of browns against a light beige background. In the foreground, there is a table with a figure standing beside it, gesturing with one arm extended. Another figure is leaning on the table, engaging in discussion. On the table are writing materials such as a pen and an inkwell. To the left, a figure is carrying a suitcase or a box. In the background, there are text phrases in French. The overall composition conveys a sense of animated interaction and communication.

artworks.title: A Foxglove in Bloom
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Rosi Schilling in memory of Edmund Schilling
artworks.description: This is a detailed line drawing of a tall plant with large, textured leaves and a flowering stalk at the top. The plant is centrally located in the drawing, with the leaves spreading outwards and the flowering stalk extending vertically from the middle of the plant. The dark lines of the drawing stand out against the paper, which is in shades of brown and appears to be aged and slightly discolored.

artworks.title: Head of the Fallen Jockey (study for "Scene from the Steeplechase: The Fallen Jockey")
artworks.medium: black chalk heightened with white on brown paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon
artworks.description: The image shows a close-up view of a person's upper body, focusing on the head and shoulders. The person is lying down, depicted in profile with the face turned upward. The facial features include a slightly open mouth, a relaxed expression, and closed eyes. The person has short, dark hair swept back from the face, and is draped in a garment covering the shoulders. There are no visible accessories or objects near the person. The background is a plain, textured surface that complements the drawing's tone and emphasizes the subject.

artworks.title: Fallen Jockey (study for "Scene from the Steeplechase: The Fallen Jockey")
artworks.medium: graphite on blue paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon
artworks.description: The image displays a sketch of a person lying down on their back. The person is reclined with arms resting by their sides, legs slightly bent at the knees. The facial features are softly drawn, with closed eyes and a peaceful expression, and the hair is short and combed back. The person is clothed in loose-fitting attire, with clear outlines of the outfit. There are no visible details of jewelry or objects held by the person in this sketch. The background is a plain, lightly toned surface.

artworks.title: Fallen Jockey (study for "Scene from the Steeplechase: The Fallen Jockey")
artworks.medium: black chalk and pastel on brown wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon
artworks.description: The image shows a drawing of a person from the knees up, lying on their back with their head tilted to the side and arms resting at their sides. The person's facial features are soft, with closed eyes and a relaxed mouth, and their medium length, slightly wavy hair is visible. They are wearing a buttoned shirt with a high collar in earthy tones with hints of red and shading, depicted with a focus on capturing the folds and textures. The background is a light, solid color, emphasizing the figure's form and posture without any additional elements.

artworks.title: Racehorses (study for "Scene from the Steeplechase: The Fallen Jockey")
artworks.medium: charcoal on light brown paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon
artworks.description: The image is a drawing of a horse in motion. The sketch features fine lines that convey speed and fluidity, depicting the dynamic posture of the horse in a full gallop. The lines are loose and black, with faint shading indicating musculature and movement. The background is simple, emphasizing the form and motion of the horse, creating a sense of immediate energy.

artworks.title: Action (Handlung)
artworks.medium: etching in black on chine collé
artworks.creditLine: Anonymous Gift
artworks.description: The image shows a man in a pinstripe suit and bow tie bending over with one arm extended, a woman in a long dress facing away, two individuals conversing, and a small dog playing or chasing something. In the background, there are dense trees, a large gazebo with ornate detailing, a railing, and round street lamps.

artworks.title: Yearnings (Wünsche)
artworks.medium: etching and aquatint in black on chine collé
artworks.creditLine: Anonymous Gift
artworks.description: The image shows a detailed scene with a blend of natural and human elements. A person is seated with their head resting in their hand, next to a lit candle on a small table. The etching style includes delicate, fine lines and cross-hatching, creating depth and texture. Tall, slender trees with small flowers extend upwards, leading towards rolling hills in the distance. The horizon is placed high in the scene, emphasizing the expansive view of the landscape and sky. The color palette is monochromatic, ranging from deep blacks to lighter grays.
